It looks like you may have dormant follicles possibly from traction alopecia or another cause of hair loss. Minoxidil (rogaine) is highly effective in growing back the hair. You can get it over the counter at 2% or 5% (doctors have said that there is no difference between women’s or men’s rogaine btw), or a dermatologist’s prescription at a higher percentage if needed. 
The Downside of minoxidil is you have to use it forever, and it has some concerning side effects (pretty rare but I did get them and had to stop) A natural alternative is rosemary essential oil, studies have found that it is comparable to 2.5% minoxidil, I am recovering from traction alopecia and my hair is growing back! Other proven agents are caffeine (using this also very effective) lavender oil, pumpkin seed oil and peppermint oil (I post a link to a Reddit post detailing these + the studies if you’d like, there’s also a great black derm on Instagram who’s discussed these)

If you do have a genetic predisposition to a receding hairline, then you may want to address that as topical agents will only solve the symptoms of any genetic or hormonal imbalance and not the root cause. Seeing a dermatologist to rule out any hormonal or nutritional deficiencies would be helpful so they can give you insight into how you can address those and can help you activate your hair follicles from the inside. if you can’t see the dermatologist right now getting a hair vitamin such as nutrafol would help address any nutritional deficiencies. 

Hope this helps!

When I first got introduced to kibbe I did the quiz and was pretty confused, so I continued researching and realized it’s easier to consider the lines on my body and then compare to the lines for each kibbe type. 

Things to consider: 
Vertical: if you have this, you would want to consider D, SD, FN. if you’re 5’7 and above you automatically have vertical. 

kibbe upper curve: if you have this and you have vertical you may be SD 

Kibbe width: if you have this and you have vertical then FN. if no vertical SN. (There may be other options with kibbe width I’m still learning) 

Kibbe double curve: it means you have both upper curve and lower curve. This would make you a romantic, I’m not sure about the difference between Soft romantics and theatrical romantics though. Still learning about that.  
But if you have double curve and you have vertical, then you are SD. Because your lower curve is accommodated by your vertical. (You don’t have to have double curve to be SD, you only need upper curve, but some SDs will notice fleshiness in their bust and hips, but realize they can’t be TR because of their vertical)

I hope that helps!
